travellingdimension.config.title: Travelling Dimension
travellingdimension.config.scope.local: Out of game: you are editing your local file. These settings will be used by your next single player world.
travellingdimension.config.scope.server: In game: these are the SERVER settings. Saving changes them for everyone.
travellingdimension.config.scope.readonl: Read only: these are the server settings, and you do not have permission to change them (level 4 required).
travellingdimension.config.restart_neede: [Travelling Dimension] A worldgen setting changed: it will only take effect on the next server start.
travellingdimension.config.denied: [Travelling Dimension] You do not have permission to change this server's configuration.
travellingdimension.config.invalid: [Travelling Dimension] Configuration refused: it is unreadable.
travellingdimension.config.option.worldg: Terrain of the travel dimension. A generator that is requested but missing falls back to vanilla, never a crash.
travellingdimension.config.option.seed.t: Seed of the dimension itself (empty = the world's seed). Choose it BEFORE the first visit: changing it later leaves visible borders between old and new chunks.
travellingdimension.config.option.largeB: Large Biomes. Consistent with the compressed ratio: biomes stay readable and crossable.
travellingdimension.config.option.custom: Registry id, for instance minecraft:amplified. Only used when the generator is Custom.
Registry id, for instance minecraft:overworld. Only used when the generator is Custom.
One block walked in the travel dimension equals this many Overworld blocks. Divide going in, multiply coming out.
travellingdimension.config.option.search: Radius, in Overworld blocks, within which an existing portal is looked for before a new one is created. The travel dimension radius follows automatically (reach divided by the ratio, so 8 blocks for 128): both describe the same square of world, and that is what guarantees a portal found on the way in still finds its partner on the way back.
travellingdimension.config.option.vertic: Full height: a portal is a candidate whatever its altitude, which makes hand built storeys usable. Bounded: the search is limited to the vertical window below.
How far above and below the ideal point to search. Ignored when the search covers the full height.

Multiplies the altitude difference in the distance calculation. 1.0 is neutral. Above that, a portal at the bottom of a cave counts as further than it is, and no longer beats a slightly more distant surface portal.
travellingdimension.config.option.frameB: Id of the block portals must be built from, for instance minecraft:amethyst_block. An unknown block falls back to the default. Choose it BEFORE building: changing it invalidates frames already placed.
travellingdimension.config.option.platfo: Id of the block poured under a created portal. Calcite by default: it is the amethyst geode's companion block and matches the frame.
How many blocks the slab extends beyond the portal, all around.
Thickness of the slab. It only replaces replaceable blocks, so anything previously built is preserved. 0 removes the platform.
travellingdimension.config.option.cleara: How wide the volume carved on each side of the portal is, so you never come out embedded in rock.
How high the volume carved above the portal is.
travellingdimension.config.option.remove: Remove water and lava from the cleared volume, so you do not arrive drowning or on fire.
travellingdimension.config.option.rememb: On the way back, come out of the exact portal you came in by. The transformation divides, so several neighbouring portals lead to the same place and no calculation alone can tell which one you took. The memory is carried by the entity and survives a restart.
travellingdimension.config.option.protec: When the footprint of a portal about to be created carries signs of building, the portal is shifted up or down to spare them. The game records nowhere who placed a block: this is therefore a presumption, built on three signals. A chunk no player has ever set foot in is treated as natural generation and nothing there is protected. Elsewhere, block entities (chests, furnaces, signs, beds) and the blocks listed in playerMadeBlocks make the portal move.
travellingdimension.config.option.buildS: How many blocks at most a portal may rise or drop to spare a build. The wanted height is tried first, then one block above, one below, and so on: the portal strays as little as possible from its ideal point. 0 disables the shift. Beyond the limit it is built anyway, and the containers moved to safety are what limits the damage.
travellingdimension.config.option.redsto: How many redstone blocks in the footprint make the ground refuse a portal, whatever else is true. Redstone is the one marker that never lies: a chest grows in a village, a machine has an author. This veto ignores the inhabited-time threshold AND the general build protection, because a machine built in a chunk the counter still thinks is untouched was otherwise invisible. When it fires, the portal looks for a free altitude across the whole world height, not just the usual 32 blocks. 0 disables the veto.
travellingdimension.config.option.rescue: Before building over them, containers in the footprint are moved to a spot drawn at random within the radius below, contents and name included. This applies whatever happens, even when the shift failed: a chest moved a few blocks beats a chest erased.
Radius, in blocks, within which a moved container is put back down. The shelter is outside the portal footprint, on ground that holds, and on a spot still free.
travellingdimension.config.option.portal: Turned off, a travel portal is 1 to 21 wide and 3 to 21 tall. Turned on, the minimum height drops to 1, so a 1x1 portal becomes possible, and the maximum becomes the setting below, up to 41. Nothing else changes: the conversion, the ideal point, the reach and the order of the ranks ignore portal size entirely. BEWARE, these bounds also revalidate a portal whenever a neighbouring block changes: turning the setting off later puts out any portal that has become out of bounds.

Maximum width and height of a travel portal, up to 41. Only has an effect when free sizes are on. A 41 wide portal is a serious piece of work: on creation the clearance and the slab follow the size, so the far end is dug out accordingly.
travellingdimension.config.option.nether: Turned off, Mojang's rule applies as it is: 2 to 21 wide, 3 to 21 tall. Turned on, an obsidian frame lights with flint and steel from 1x1 up to the maximum set below. This is the only setting in the mod that alters vanilla's shape detection, so the rule applies to EVERY Nether portal in the world. It also governs the size copied on the far side: a 1x1 arch is answered by a 1x1 arch. BEWARE, these bounds also revalidate a portal: turning the setting off later puts out any portal that has become out of bounds.
Maximum width and height of a Nether portal, up to 41. Only has an effect when Nether free sizes are on.
travellingdimension.config.option.portal: Dye ties two travel portals together: among the portals within reach, only those matching the colour of the portal you left are considered, and the nearest of those wins. Nothing is refused, dye as many portals the same colour as you like. Turned off, dye has no effect and colours already placed are ignored, but they stay in the save: turning it back on puts them straight back to work. Twin of the Nether portal setting, the two switch off separately.

Lets any player lock a portal with /tdlock. A locked portal forbids LIGHTING another portal within its territory, that is within the search reach: 128 blocks in the Overworld, 8 in the travel dimension. The player who tries gets a message naming the owner and giving the coordinates. The automatic creation the mod performs when a traveller arrives is never blocked: they have to land somewhere.
travellingdimension.config.option.nether: Nether portals at the ideal point

The game does not build the Nether portal where the maths sends it: it looks for a spot it deems suitable, and the portal can end up far from the computed point. On, it is built at the exact coordinate and the terrain adapts instead: clearance around, platform below, with the same settings as the travel dimension. The frame stays obsidian and the axis stays vanilla's. No portal is ever created above the Nether roof: that floor belongs to the players who build there by hand. Off, the game behaves exactly as usual.

The Nether portal that gets created copies the width and height of the one you walked through, the way the travel dimension does. Vanilla always builds a 2x3, the minimum size: a 9 wide arch answers with a 2 wide slot, and large mobs no longer fit. Off, the size stays vanilla's. No effect when Nether portals at the ideal point is off: the game does the building then.

Extends the dye mechanic to ordinary Nether portals. Vanilla's algorithm is untouched: when two portals of the same colour answer each other, the mod only says which of the portals vanilla would have found is kept. Vanilla reach: 16 blocks in the Nether, 128 in the Overworld, which is the same square of world on both sides. With no colour placed, nothing changes.
travellingdimension.config.option.struct: Villages, dungeons and the like in the travel dimension. Only affects chunks not generated yet.
travellingdimension.config.option.mobDen: Multiplier on spawn caps, in the travel dimension only. 1.0 = normal.
travellingdimension.config.option.logFal: Write to the logs when the requested generator is missing and the mod falls back to vanilla.
